title: Fort Ville-Marie

terrainReference.basis: Present-day open elevation at the historical model anchor.

mapIdentity.provider: Pointe-à-Callière excavation summary and mapped modern site control
mapIdentity.scope: Archaeological excavations at 214 Place D’Youville and the 2015 sidewalk trench establish the historic site. Pointe-à-Callière describes about 2,500 square metres in a rectangular plan oriented roughly parallel to the Saint Lawrence, with four timber bastions. The geographic control comes from the current excavated parcel and current nearby river-edge axis. The footprint is a constrained reconstruction.

note: The museum and archaeology literature confirm the palisade trench, possible guardhouse, stone foundations for metallurgical work and 1658 timber-lined well. The McGill catalogue’s written description of Bourdon’s early manuscript lists the chapel and magazine. Morin’s later drawing provides general placement and roof cues, with the excavated timber enclosure taking precedence. Heights and complete building placement are estimates.
